question_text:
The exponential function $y = a \times 2^x + b$ passes through the points alongside:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\\hline y & 20 & p & 35 & q \\\hline\end{array}$$

subparts.stem: Write down two linear equations which could be used to determine the values of $a$ and $b$.
subparts.solution:
When $x = 0$, $y = 20$
$\therefore 20 = a \times 2^0 + b$
$\therefore a + b = 20$ .... (1)
When $x = 2$, $y = 35$
$\therefore 35 = a \times 2^2 + b$
$\therefore 4a + b = 35$ .... (2)

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Substitute given $(x, y)$ coordinate pairs into the model equation $y = a \times 2^x + b$ to form a system of linear equations.
step_by_step: For $x = 0$, $y = 20$: $a \times 2^0 + b = 20 \implies a(1) + b = 20 \implies a + b = 20$.

subparts.stem: Solve the linear equations simultaneously to find $a$ and $b$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Express $b$ in terms of $a$ and substitute into the second equation

subparts.solution:
Using (1), $b = 20 - a$ .... (3)
Substituting $b = 20 - a$ into (2) gives
$4a + 20 - a = 35$
$\therefore 3a = 15$
$\therefore a = 5$
Substituting $a = 5$ into (3) gives $b = 20 - 5 = 15$
$\therefore a = 5 \text{ and } b = 15$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Solve the simultaneous linear equations using substitution or elimination.
step_by_step: Subtract equation (1) from equation (2): $(4a + b) - (a + b) = 35 - 20$.

subparts.stem: Hence find the values of $p$ and $q$.
subparts.solution:
Using b, $y = 5 \times 2^x + 15$
When $x = 1$, $y = p$
$\therefore p = 5 \times 2^1 + 15$
$\therefore p = 25$
When $x = 3$, $y = q$
$\therefore q = 5 \times 2^3 + 15$
$\therefore q = 55$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Substitute the values of $a$ and $b$ to complete the function, then substitute $x = 1$ and $x = 3$ to find the corresponding $y$-values.
